clue.text: The strong hold taken by Cronin's publisher

definitions.meaning: a fortress or stronghold guarding a city, with the article
the title of A. J. Cronin's 1937 novel about a doctor, which his publisher took on

explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress commanding a city, and it is also the title of Cronin's best-known novel.

clue.text: James Wormold sold vacuum cleaners there

definitions.text: James Wormold sold vacuum cleaners there

parts.words: James Wormold sold vacuum cleaners there
parts.note: Graham Greene's hero of Our Man in ... is a vacuum-cleaner salesman in the Cuban capital who is recruited as a spy

explanation.surface: A man named James Wormold once made a living selling vacuum cleaners somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cuban capital is the setting of Greene's spy comedy in which Wormold runs his vacuum-cleaner shop.

clue.text: Playwright seen to study Greek the day before…

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
an eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: A dramatist is spotted studying Greek on the eve of something, the dots leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link this clue to 4-down, but each stands alone; 'seen to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: William Congreve was the Restoration dramatist who wrote The Way of the World.

clue.text: … these opportunities were offered by Fletcher

definitions.text: these opportunities were offered by Fletcher

parts.words: these opportunities were offered by Fletcher
parts.note: John Fletcher, the Jacobean dramatist, wrote a comedy whose title is a phrase for these openings

explanation.surface: Continuing from the dramatist before, a man named Fletcher offers some opportunities.
explanation.definitionFit: Fletcher's comedy of about 1617 carries this title, which also simply means these opportunities.

clue.text: Clotho's life source from underworld river

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and the name of the underworld itself
the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff in Wales

explanation.surface: The Fate who spins life seems to draw her thread from a river of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link. Clotho is the Fate who spins the thread of each life on the staff that holds the wool.
explanation.definitionFit: Clotho spins the thread of life from the spinning staff that holds the unspun fibre.

clue.text: Deighton's amusement in popular fiction

indicators.note: the word in tells us the letters sit inside the phrase popular fiction

explanation.surface: Len Deighton's idea of fun shows up in his popular fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Len Deighton's novel Only When I ... uses this comic spelling of the slang pronunciation of a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic spelling of a laugh in the title of Deighton's novel Only When I ... means a bit of fun.

clue.text: A muse hot for Racine's queen

parts.note: Thalia is the Muse of comedy
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A Muse swapped for a queen in a French tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. Racine's last tragedy is named after this biblical queen of Judah.
explanation.definitionFit: Racine's last tragedy, Athalie, is about the biblical queen of Judah of this name.

clue.text: Coward associates them with the rabid

definitions.text: Coward associates them with the rabid

parts.words: Coward associates them with the rabid
parts.note: Noel Coward's song couples mad dogs with these people, who go out in the midday sun

explanation.surface: A timid person links some people with mad animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coward' looks like a timid person, but it is Noel Coward, whose song is Mad Dogs and ..., the rabid being the mad dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Coward's song says only mad dogs and the natives of England go out in the midday sun.

clue.text: A sort of chamberlain and novelist

definitions.meaning: Sir ... Chamberlain was the British Foreign Secretary, one of the Chamberlain family, so a first name marks one sort of Chamberlain
Jane, author of Pride and Prejudice

explanation.definitionFit: Austen Chamberlain was a statesman of the Chamberlain family, and Jane Austen the novelist shares the name.

clue.text: One of them is time, Byron thought

definitions.text: One of them is time, Byron thought

parts.words: One of them is time, Byron thought
parts.note: in Childe Harold Byron addresses Time as the beautifier of the dead and the one who takes revenge

explanation.surface: Byron reckoned that time belongs to some group or other.
explanation.definitionFit: Byron's line 'O Time! the beautifier of the dead... Time, the avenger!' makes time one who takes revenge.

clue.text: A stern guard for Captain Dorling

definitions.meaning: the rail round the stern of a ship
Captain Henry Taprell Dorling wrote naval stories under a pen name taken from this ship fitting

explanation.definitionFit: The rail at a ship's stern gave its name as pen name to the naval writer Captain Dorling.

clue.text: Poison given a certain value by Mary Webb

definitions.text: given a certain value by Mary Webb
definitions.meaning: Mary Webb's novel is Precious ..., which gives the word a value

explanation.definitionFit: The word means poison or ruin, and Mary Webb's novel calls it Precious, a value indeed.

clue.text: Awfully big brained Liverpool writer

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters are badly jumbled, and nods to her novel An Awfully Big Adventure

explanation.surface: A Liverpool writer is said to be terribly clever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges BIG BRAINED; it also recalls Beryl Bainbridge's novel An Awfully Big Adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl Bainbridge, the novelist, was born in Liverpool.

clue.text: Sign of affection to Irish poet. From a Scottish one

parts.note: AE was the pen name of the Irish poet George William Russell
a fond kiss is a loving gesture

explanation.surface: A loving gesture goes to an Irish poet, and comes from a Scottish one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link. 'one' in the definition means a poem: Robert Burns's song of parting.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Burns, the Scottish poet, wrote this farewell song beginning with a parting kiss.

clue.text: Subsequently gratify a Larkin poem

parts.note: subsequently means next, coming after
to gratify is to please

explanation.surface: Later on, keep someone happy with a poem by Larkin.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin's poem in The Less Deceived carries this title about waiting for what comes.

clue.text: His dramatic output was absurd

parts.note: the playwright is the leading figure of the Theatre of the Absurd, so his plays were absurd in the technical sense

explanation.surface: Someone's plays were simply ridiculous.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene Ionesco wrote The Bald Prima Donna and Rhinoceros, key works of the Theatre of the Absurd.

clue.text: Diary of Hermann Broch's eponymous wanderers?

definitions.text: Diary of Hermann Broch's eponymous wanderers?

parts.words: Diary of Hermann Broch's eponymous wanderers?
parts.note: Broch's trilogy is The Sleepwalkers, night wanderers, whose journal would be a record of night

explanation.surface: A journal kept by the title characters of a novel by Hermann Broch.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a record of what happens by night, fit for sleepwalkers who wander then.

clue.text: Cattle and cured meat for Kingsley adventurer

parts.note: oxen are cattle
ham is cured meat from a pig's leg

explanation.surface: Cattle and bacon are served up for a hero of Charles Kingsley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'for' are links. John Oxenham is a sea adventurer in Charles Kingsley's Westward Ho!
explanation.definitionFit: John Oxenham is the Elizabethan sea adventurer who appears in Kingsley's Westward Ho!

clue.text: A role like Hamlet, or The Hobbit

definitions.text: A role like Hamlet, or The Hobbit

parts.words: A role like Hamlet, or The Hobbit
parts.note: the character whose name is the title of the play or book is the title role

explanation.surface: A part such as the Prince of Denmark, or Bilbo in The Hobbit.
explanation.definitionFit: A title role, the character named in the work's title, as Hamlet or the hobbit.

clue.text: Ancient rulers fit into frames essentially too elaborate for them

indicators.note: fit into tells us the letters sit within the words frames essentially

explanation.surface: Ancient kings could be fitted into frames, but they were too grand for them.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'frames essentially'; 'too elaborate for them' completes the picture of pharaohs being too grand for a frame.
explanation.definitionFit: Rameses was the name of several Egyptian pharaohs, so the plural means ancient kings.

clue.text: Mrs Crawley displays Rebecca's stringed instrument (5, )

parts.note: Becky is a pet form of Rebecca, and the possessive gives an S
a harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A married woman shows off the harp that belongs to Rebecca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displays' is a link. Thackeray's Becky Sharp in Vanity Fair becomes Mrs Rawdon Crawley.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's adventuress in Vanity Fair marries Rawdon Crawley, so she is Mrs Crawley.

clue.text: Novelist gives direction to humankind

parts.note: man means humankind
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A novelist gives the human race some guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives ... to' is a link: the direction is added to humankind.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Mann, author of The Magic Mountain, was a German novelist.

clue.text: Clumsily reined nymph

indicators.note: clumsily says the letters of reined are handled awkwardly and rearranged

explanation.surface: A sea nymph pulls on the reins awkwardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nereid is one of the sea nymphs, daughters of Nereus.

clue.text: "I say — Ireland with Indian corn and good wheat." (Cobden)

definitions.text: "I say — Ireland with Indian corn and good wheat." (Cobden)

parts.words: "I say — Ireland with Indian corn and good wheat." (Cobden)
parts.note: Richard Cobden, the corn-law reformer, urged that Ireland be flooded with cheap grain; the dash marks the missing verb

explanation.surface: Cobden says Ireland should get maize and good wheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To flood or swamp, as Cobden wished to flood famine Ireland with cheap grain.

clue.text: Assistant initiates analysis in Dickens essay

indicators.note: initiates means the starting letters of the words analysis in Dickens essay

explanation.surface: A helper starts analysing an essay on Dickens.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant.

clue.text: Conditions improving, we hear, for OE

indicators.note: we hear tells us the words are spoken and a similar-sounding word is meant

parts.note: when the weather at sea gets better, the sea is fairer

explanation.surface: Weather getting better, they say, for a poem in Old English.
explanation.walkthrough: OE is Old English; The Seafarer is an Old English elegy, so the poem is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seafarer is the Old English elegy in the Exeter Book about a sailor's lonely life.

clue.text: Everybody had heard of him since his "duel with six fencing master"

definitions.text: Everybody had heard of him since his "duel with six fencing master"

parts.words: Everybody had heard of him since his "duel with six fencing master"
parts.note: Conan Doyle's Brigadier of that name boasts of fighting six fencing masters in a single duel

explanation.surface: A man is famous for a duel against six fencing masters.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's boastful Brigadier, the Napoleonic hussar, tells of his duel with six fencing masters.

clue.text: Season for white geans, thought Housman

definitions.text: Season for white geans, thought Housman

parts.words: Season for white geans, thought Housman
parts.note: geans are wild cherries; Housman's cherry tree stands wearing white for this time of year

explanation.surface: Housman pictured a time of year when the wild cherries are white.
explanation.definitionFit: Housman's Loveliest of trees is wearing white for the weeks after the spring festival.
